"Clout" is a word with more than one meaning depending on the context. Here's everything you need to know.
The Most Important Meaning: Power and Influence

This is the meaning you'll encounter most often today. When someone has clout, they have the power to make things happen, influence decisions, or get results — not because of a formal title or rule, but because of who they are, who they know, or what they represent.

Think of it as the invisible weight a person carries. Someone with clout walks into a room and people listen. They can make a phone call and get something done that ordinary people can't. They can push an idea forward, open doors, or protect others from consequences.

Examples:

  • "She has a lot of clout in the film industry." (People in Hollywood take her seriously and listen to her.)
  • "He used his political clout to get the project approved." (His influence in politics helped move things forward.)
  • "The union lost clout after the strike failed." (The union's power to pressure employers became weaker.)

Clout in this sense is usually earned — through experience, reputation, money, status, or a combination of all of these. It is informal power, not written-down authority. A CEO has official authority. A retired legend in the same field might have clout — people defer to them not because they have to, but because they respect and fear their influence.

Importantly, clout is only real if others acknowledge it. You can't claim clout for yourself — others grant it to you through their behavior.
The Second Meaning: A Hard Hit

"Clout" can also mean a heavy, forceful blow — usually from a hand. This usage is more common in British and Irish English, and in older literature. You might see it less often today, but it still appears in informal speech.

Examples:

  • "He gave the door a clout and it swung open."
  • "She got a clout on the ear from her older brother."
The Modern Internet Meaning: Online Fame

In recent years, especially among younger generations, "clout" has developed a specific meaning in the world of social media and internet culture. Here, clout means online fame, popularity, or social status — the kind measured in followers, likes, viral moments, and public recognition.

If someone is said to have clout on the internet, it means they are widely known, respected, or followed online. Their posts get attention. Their opinions shape trends. Their endorsement of something gives it value.

Examples:

  • "She built her clout by posting daily on social media for two years."
  • "He's one of the most influential voices online — the man has serious clout."

This is really just the same core idea as the first meaning (power and influence), but applied specifically to the social media world. It's still about the ability to affect people and be taken seriously — it's just that the arena is the internet rather than politics or business.

Because clout is so desirable, a very common expression has formed around it: clout chasing. This means doing something — often embarrassing, controversial, or attention-grabbing — purely to gain fame, followers, or recognition, rather than out of genuine belief or talent. A "clout chaser" is someone who craves social currency and will do almost anything to get it.

Example:

  • "He got into that fake argument just for attention. Classic clout chaser."

Clout chasing carries a negative tone. It implies the person is being fake, opportunistic, or desperate.
How "Clout" Feels Compared to Similar Words

Understanding a word also means knowing how it feels compared to words that seem similar:

  • Clout vs. Power — Power is a broad, neutral word. Clout is more specific — it's informal, earned through reputation, and often personal. A president has power. A beloved community elder has clout.
  • Clout vs. Fame — Fame means being known by many people. Clout means that your being known actually affects things. A famous actor has fame. If directors compete to cast them, they have clout.
  • Clout vs. Prestige — Prestige is about being respected and admired. Clout is more action-oriented — it's about actually being able to do things with that respect.
The Single Thread Running Through All Meanings

Whether you're talking about political influence, a hard punch, or Instagram fame, there is one idea connecting all uses of "clout" as a noun: force. Something with clout carries weight — it hits hard, whether that's literally (a blow) or figuratively (the impact a powerful person can have).

So when you hear or read the word "clout," always ask: who has the weight here, and what are they doing with it?
